instructions:
# Paprika: guide for agents

Document = flat map of nodes + rootIds (top-level screens/frames, in canvas coordinates).
Types: frame (container with style and layout), group (groups without painting), page (separate canvas), rect, ellipse,
text, image, path (vector with bezier curves), shape (diagram shape with text inside), connector (line/arrow between
nodes). Only frame, group and page have children.

Common fields: name, x, y, width, height (number | "hug" | "fill"), rotation, opacity (0..1),
visible, locked, layoutPositioning ("auto"|"absolute", omit = auto), fill (color), stroke {color, width: n | "$token"}, radius (n | "$token", or on frame, rect and image [tl, tr, br, bl] with each corner n | "$token"), shadow (one object or a list of up to 8: {x, y, blur, spread: n | "$token", color, inner?}), outline {color, width: n | "$token", style?: solid|dashed|dotted, offset?}, filter and backdropFilter {blur?: n | "$token", saturate? 0..10, grayscale? 0..1, brightness? 0..10, sepia? 0..1, invert? 0..1, hueRotate? -360..360}, notes, lintIgnore (rule names lint_design skips on this node).
frame: clip (bool), layout {mode: none|row|column, gap (n | "$token"), padding (one number or [top, right, bottom, left]; each n | "$token"; not two values), align: start|center|end|stretch,
  justify: start|center|end|between, wrap}, scaledMock (true: a scaled mock, lint_design skips small-text inside it), mode (theme mode, see below). With row/column layout, children's x/y are ignored unless layoutPositioning is "absolute" (the child keeps x/y relative to the parent and is skipped by flow, gap and hug). Omit it or set "auto" to stay in the flow.
text: text, color, fontFamily, fontSize (n | "$token"), fontWeight (100..900), lineHeight (n | "$token"), letterSpacing (n | "$token"), textAlign.
  Without width/height a new text hugs its content ("hug" on both axes); give width to wrap lines.
image: src (https:// or data:image/), fit (cover|contain|fill), alt.
group: name, x, y, opacity, visible, locked, notes, children. The box (x, y, width, height) is computed from the
  children at the end of each write; children's coordinates are relative to the group. Use group_nodes/ungroup_nodes.
page: name, fill (canvas background), mode, notes, children. Top level only; once there are pages, every top-level node
  is a page and frames go in parentId = the page id (canvas coordinates). create_page creates the first one and moves
  the current content to "Página 1". create_page {ensure: true, name} returns the existing page of that name instead of creating another. Screens of another page: get_document_outline {rootId: page id}.
Components: a frame with component: true is a component (create_component). An instance is a frame with
  instanceOf = the component id and an optional scale (create_instance): its children are generated copies, with
  derived ids and sourceId = the id of the source node; changing the component changes every instance. On a copy,
  update only changes fill, color, text, src, alt, visible and opacity (stored as an instance override; null goes back
  to the component); on the root, fill becomes an override and width/height/layout/stroke/radius/shadow/clip come from
  the component (use scale). Copies cannot be moved, deleted or given children: edit the component or detach_instance.
path: d (SVG path data: M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute or relative), fill (no fill = outline only),
  stroke {color,width}, fillRule (nonzero|evenodd), strokeCap (butt|round|square), strokeJoin (miter|round|bevel),
  optional viewBox [x,y,w,h]. Without viewBox, d's coordinates are px from the node's (x,y) corner; with viewBox,
  the drawing is scaled to fit width×height (good for icons on a 24×24 grid). Without width/height, the node
  gets the drawing's box. Curves: "C c1x c1y c2x c2y x y" (cubic), "Q cx cy x y" (quadratic), S/T mirror the
  previous control point (smooth curves). Use get_bounds (absolute boxes + rotated corners), path_info to check bounds before positioning.
shape: shape (rect|ellipse|diamond|triangle|note), text (centered; top-left on a note), color, fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight,
  lineHeight, textAlign. width/height are numbers (default 160×80; note 160×160). fill/stroke/radius/shadow paint the
  outline; fields left out on create get the kind's defaults (white with a dark border; note = yellow sticky note).
connector: from/to = {nodeId, side?: auto|top|right|bottom|left} (attached to a node) or {x, y} (free point in the
  parent's coordinates), route (straight|elbow|rounded|curve), radius (rounded corners), control {x,y} (curve handle in parent coords), startArrow/endArrow (none|arrow), stroke {color,width}, dashed,
  label (text halfway along the route, in the stroke color: "yes", "no").
  x, y, width, height and d are computed from the ends at every write (read-only): moving a shape redraws its
  connectors, and deleting a node deletes the connectors attached to it.
Diagrams: draw_diagram takes nodes (shapes) + edges (connectors) and lays out the shapes without x/y for you.

Colors: #hex, rgb(), rgba() or "$token" (see set_tokens). Prefer tokens for recurring colors and sizes.
Theme modes: set_tokens with mode ("dark", "compact"…) writes only the tokens that change; "mode" on a frame or page applies the mode to its subtree (the same screen can sit light and dark side by side). export_code with cssVariables: true writes var(--token) and one rule per mode.
"fill" in width/height takes the remaining space on the main axis of a parent with layout, or stretches on the cross axis.

Placement: a new top-level frame leaves x and y unset (or passes place:"free") and lands in free space, to the right of the page content, same top, gap 80, wrapping to a new row past 2400px from the content's left. place is "free" | "below" | "right" | {near, side: left|right|above|below} | "none" (exact x/y). Concurrent writers never share a spot. get_document_outline and get_bounds with no ids report the page content box and the next free spot. Draw overlays (modals, menus, toasts) last, or bring them to the front with index:"front". A write warns when a new top-level node overlaps another and names the nearest free spot.

Pins: the human can point at a node or an area of the canvas and write what to do there ("Point for the AI"). Call list_pins first when the human mentions pins, and whenever a write result carries openPins; claim_pin before working on one, resolve_pin with a short reply when done. wait_for_pins waits for new ones.

Recommended flow:
1. get_document_outline to get your bearings (cheap).
2. set_tokens with the palette and the type scale.
3. create_nodes with nested trees (children) in one call; prefer frames with layout over absolute positioning.
4. lint_design and fix whatever comes back as error/warning. rootIds (or rootId) lints only those subtrees. groups folds each rule to a count and the first maxIds node ids (default 8), ordered by severity; issues still lists every finding. minSeverity (info|warning|error) drops quieter findings. minFontSize raises the small-text floor (default 12). A frame with scaledMock, or lintIgnore on a node, keeps intentional small type and literal colors out of the list.
5. render_screenshot to check visually; export_image for PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF/PDF without Chromium; export_code to take it to code.
To bring in a ready icon or a piece of a page, use import_svg or import_html (they become editable nodes), import_image for a PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or GIF file; export_code with format "svg" returns vector SVG.
Every write is atomic (all or nothing) and can be undone with undo. To make several calls one undo step (e.g. "draw proposal 3"), pass the same batch to each of them; the batch closes when anyone else writes or undoes in between.
Results: JSON tools also return structuredContent that matches their outputSchema; read it instead of parsing the text.
Workspaces: the server holds several documents (list_workspaces). Document tools take an optional workspaceId and read or write that workspace without open_workspace and without moving the human's canvas; omit workspaceId to use the active workspace. The outline's first line and every write result include that workspace's id and name. Undo and redo take the same workspaceId and revert only that workspace; each workspace keeps its own history for the life of the process. Edits to the workspace the canvas is showing arrive live; edits to another workspace do not switch the canvas. open_workspace still switches the active workspace for everyone, so ask the human first; create_workspace makes an empty one, rename_workspace renames one, set_workspace_cover puts an image (or a screenshot of a frame) on its card; archive_workspace hides one from list_workspaces without deleting it (the active one hands over to the most recently updated other workspace that is not archived; the only one cannot be archived) and unarchive_workspace brings it back; opening an archived workspace unarchives it; list_workspaces omits archived workspaces unless includeArchived is true, and each workspace reports archived; delete_workspace cannot be undone and takes two calls: the first, without confirmToken, returns a summary of what would be lost and a short-lived token; show that summary to the human and only call again with the token after they agree. list_workspace_ops reads who created, renamed, opened, archived, unarchived or deleted a workspace, and a delete entry keeps its summary.
The human sees your edits live on the canvas. Unknown fields are rejected with an error: read the message and adjust.
This guide in Brazilian Portuguese: get_design_guide {language: "pt-BR"}.

tools.name: get_design_guide
tools.title: Format guide
tools.description: Explains the node model, the accepted fields and the recommended flow. Read it before the first edit. language: "pt-BR" returns the Brazilian Portuguese version.

tools.name: get_document_outline
tools.title: Document outline
tools.description: Compact tree (one line per node: type#id, name, size, position, key style), tokens, theme modes and version. The first line names the workspace id and name. The last lines are the page content box and the next free spot. Cheap in tokens.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

tools.name: get_nodes
tools.title: Read nodes
tools.description: Full JSON of the requested nodes (every field, with defaults). The text result is the array; structuredContent is { nodes }.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

tools.name: get_bounds
tools.title: Resolved geometry
tools.description: Absolute boxes for nodes after auto-layout (row/column, hug/fill), with transform origin and the four corners after rotation. Optional `ids` filters the result; optional `rootId` limits to that subtree (still resolves ancestors for flex). Without both, returns every node on the current page. With no ids, also returns the page content box and the next free spot.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

content.description: Page content box. Present when ids is omitted.

next.description: Top-left of the next free spot. Present when ids is omitted.

tools.name: find_nodes
tools.title: Find nodes
tools.description: Search by type, or by a substring of the name or the text, optionally inside a subtree.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

tools.name: path_info
tools.title: Path geometry
tools.description: Validates SVG path data (d) and returns the exact box of the drawing (including the extremes of bezier curves and arcs), the drawing `origin` (offset from the node origin to the path bounds), the number of segments and d normalized to absolute commands. Pass `d` or the `id` of a path node; with `id` also returns canvasBounds, transformOrigin and rotated corners.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

canvasBounds.description: With id: the box in canvas coordinates

origin.description: Offset from the node origin (0,0) to the drawing's top-left (use normalize:true on create to clear it)

transformOrigin.description: With id: CSS transform-origin (box centre) in canvas coordinates

corners.description: With id: the four corners after rotation (TL, TR, BR, BL)

tools.name: create_nodes
tools.title: Create nodes
tools.description: Creates one or more nodes (with nested children in frames) under parentId (null/omitted = canvas). Atomic. Returns {ids, roots, created, version}: ids is every new id (the previous created list); roots is each new node whose parent was not created in this call, as {id, name, type, x, y, width, height}; created is every new node as {id, name, type, parentId}. The text is that JSON plus one readable line per root. On a connector, x, y, width, height and d follow from/to: if a copied node carries them, create_nodes ignores those fields and says so in warnings. On a path, `normalize: true` moves the drawing to (0,0) and adds the previous offset to x/y so the node box matches the ink. place puts each root: "free" (default for a top-level node with no x/y, to the right of the page content, same top, gap 80, wrapping past 2400px), "below", "right", {near, side}, or "none" for the exact x/y.

index.description: Position among the siblings; default: at the end

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

place.description: Where new roots go. "free" (default for a top-level node with no x/y: right of the page content, same top, gap 80, wrap past 2400px) | "below" | "right" | {near, side: left|right|above|below} | "none" (exact x/y).

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: update_nodes
tools.title: Update nodes
tools.description: Changes fields of several nodes in one atomic transaction. null removes a field. Objects (layout, stroke, shadow, outline, filter, backdropFilter) are replaced whole. shadow is one object or a list of up to 8. The pseudo-field index (a number, 0 = the back, or "front", "back", "forward", "backward") reorders the node in its current parent — same call, same undo step.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: delete_nodes
tools.title: Delete nodes
tools.description: Deletes nodes and their subtrees. Atomic, and undo brings them back. Returns {deleted, version}: every id removed, including subtrees and the connectors attached to them.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: move_nodes
tools.title: Move nodes
tools.description: Changes the parent and/or the order of nodes (parentId null = canvas). Does not change x/y. index is the position in the new parent (0 = the back) or a step: "front", "back", "forward", "backward".

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: group_nodes
tools.title: Group nodes
tools.description: Puts sibling nodes (same parent, no row/column layout) in a new group, in the place of the topmost one. The drawing does not move: the group's box follows its children. Returns the group id.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: combine_paths
tools.title: Boolean path combine
tools.description: Combines 2+ path, rect, ellipse or shape siblings into one path via union, subtract, intersect or exclude. Keeps the bottom-most node's style, deletes the sources, one undo step. Returns the new path id. Canvas UI for this is separate.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: ungroup_nodes
tools.title: Ungroup
tools.description: Removes groups: their children go back to the group's parent, in its place, keeping position, opacity and visibility.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: create_page
tools.title: Create page
tools.description: Creates a page (a separate canvas in the same file). The first time, the current content first moves to a page named "Page 1". Create screens on it with create_nodes {parentId: page id}. Returns {page, created, version}: `page` is the new page's id; `created` lists every page made, in order (the first call also makes "Page 1"). With ensure: true and a name, returns the existing page of that name instead of creating a second one (`ensured`: true, `created` empty, version unchanged).

ensure.description: When true and a page with this name already exists, return that page instead of creating another

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

ensured.description: True when ensure found an existing page and nothing was created

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: create_component
tools.title: Create component
tools.description: Marks a frame as a component (component: true). Then create_instance makes copies of it that follow the changes to the component.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: create_instance
tools.title: Create instance
tools.description: Creates an instance of a component (a frame with instanceOf). By default it goes in the component's parent, 40px to its right. Returns the instance id and, in copies, the id of the copy of each component node (for overrides with update_nodes).

parentId.description: Parent of the instance (default: the component's parent)

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: detach_instance
tools.title: Detach instance
tools.description: Turns instances into plain frames: the copies become normal nodes (same ids) and stop following the component.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: apply_ops
tools.title: Operation transaction
tools.description: Applies a mixed list of operations (create, update, delete, move, set_tokens, rename_document, group, ungroup, add_page, detach, combine_paths) in one atomic transaction.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: set_tokens
tools.title: Set tokens
tools.description: Creates or updates design tokens (colors, sizes). Use them in nodes as "$name". null removes one. With `mode`, writes the values of that theme mode (e.g. "dark"), which apply in frames/pages with the same `mode` and their descendants; tokens the mode does not define use the base value.

mode.description: Theme mode ([A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}); without it, the base tokens

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: undo
tools.title: Undo
tools.description: Undoes the last transaction (from any author: agent or human) in the workspace given by workspaceId, or in the active one when it is omitted. Does not switch the canvas. A batch is undone whole.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: redo
tools.title: Redo
tools.description: Redoes the last undone transaction in the workspace given by workspaceId, or in the active one when it is omitted. Does not switch the canvas.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: get_history
tools.title: History
tools.description: Latest transactions (author, label, time, number of ops). Shows what the human changed on the canvas. The text result is the array; structuredContent is { entries }.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List workspaces
tools.description: Workspaces this server can open (each one is a document), most recently updated first, and which one is active. Archived workspaces are hidden unless includeArchived is true; each workspace reports archived. Every other tool reads and writes the active workspace, the same one the human sees on the canvas. An archived workspace can still be read or written by id.

includeArchived.description: When true, include archived workspaces. Omitted or false, they are hidden.

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the last write

cover.description: URL of the cover image (served by this server), or null: the overview card shows the first letter of the name

archived.description: True when the workspace is archived and hidden from the default list

tools.name: list_workspace_ops
tools.title: Workspace operations log
tools.description: Workspace operations in this server: create, rename, open, archive, unarchive and delete, each with who acted ("user" for the canvas and its HTTP API, or the agent's name over MCP), when, and which workspace. Newest first, optionally narrowed to one workspace. A delete entry carries the same summary delete_workspace returns, which is what a canvas notice shows. Entries outlive the workspace they name. This is not the document's undo history: that is get_history.

workspaceId.description: only operations of this workspace (from list_workspaces)

actor.description: "user" or the agent name that acted

workspaceName.description: the name at the time of the operation

detail.description: rename: {from}; import: {source:"import"}; delete: the WorkspaceDeletion summary; otherwise {}

tools.name: open_workspace
tools.title: Open workspace
tools.description: Makes another workspace the active one: every tool and the human's canvas switch to it, and undo history starts from that workspace. Tell the human before switching away from what they are looking at.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the last write

cover.description: URL of the cover image (served by this server), or null: the overview card shows the first letter of the name

archived.description: True when the workspace is archived and hidden from the default list

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.title: Create workspace
tools.description: Creates an empty workspace. It does not become active: call open_workspace to work in it.

name.description: Workspace name, shown on the overview (blank: "Untitled")

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the last write

cover.description: URL of the cover image (served by this server), or null: the overview card shows the first letter of the name

archived.description: True when the workspace is archived and hidden from the default list

tools.name: import_document
tools.title: Import document
tools.description: Stores a .paprika.json document (written by paprika export or paprika export --root) as a new workspace on this server. It does not become active: the human's canvas and every other tool keep working in the current workspace until open_workspace. A document whose id already exists here is stored as a copy with a new document id (node ids are kept). place is "none": the file is its own workspace and keeps its coordinates. To place artwork on the current page, use import_svg, import_html or import_image.

document.description: the .paprika.json document object (format paprika/1), read from the file

name.description: workspace name override (default: the document's name)

place.description: Where new roots go. "free" (default for a top-level node with no x/y: right of the page content, same top, gap 80, wrap past 2400px) | "below" | "right" | {near, side: left|right|above|below} | "none" (exact x/y).

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the last write

cover.description: URL of the cover image (served by this server), or null: the overview card shows the first letter of the name

active.description: id of the workspace that stays active (the import never switches it)

tools.name: rename_workspace
tools.title: Rename workspace
tools.description: Renames a workspace (the name shown on the overview). Renaming the active one is an undoable write (rename_document); any other is renamed in place.

name.description: New name (trimmed, must not be blank)

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the last write

cover.description: URL of the cover image (served by this server), or null: the overview card shows the first letter of the name

archived.description: True when the workspace is archived and hidden from the default list

tools.name: archive_workspace
tools.title: Archive workspace
tools.description: Hides a workspace from list_workspaces without deleting it. The document, history and cover stay. Archiving the active workspace first opens the most recently updated other workspace that is not archived. The only visible workspace cannot be archived. Archiving one that is already archived changes nothing.

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the last write

cover.description: URL of the cover image (served by this server), or null: the overview card shows the first letter of the name

archived.description: True when the workspace is archived and hidden from the default list

active.description: Id of the workspace that is active afterwards

tools.name: unarchive_workspace
tools.title: Unarchive workspace

tools.name: delete_workspace
tools.title: Delete workspace
tools.description: Deletes a workspace for good, in two calls. Without confirmToken nothing is deleted: the result is a summary of what would be lost (name, node/page/frame/image/connector counts, stored undo entries, the last edit, whether it has a cover, and which workspace would become active) plus a short-lived confirmToken tied to that workspace id. Show that summary to the human, and call again with the token only after they agree. The token is single-use and expires in about two minutes; reusing it or sending one for another workspace is refused with an actionable error. Deleting the active workspace first opens the most recently updated other one for everyone, and the only workspace cannot be deleted.

tools.name: lint_design
tools.title: Review design
tools.description: Checks WCAG AA contrast, missing tokens and theme modes, overflow, small or empty text, images without alt, colors outside the tokens, row/column children that leave their frame, a default 100×100 layout frame (hug-was-meant), geometry (siblings that do not touch, gaps under 4px, fully hidden shapes), overlapping boards and text covered by an overlay. rootIds (or rootId) lints only those subtrees. groups folds each rule to a count and the first maxIds node ids (default 8), ordered by severity. minSeverity drops quieter findings. minFontSize raises the small-text floor (default 12).

rootIds.description: Lint only these subtrees, so parallel work does not see other frames.

tools.name: render_screenshot
tools.title: Screenshot
tools.description: PNG of a node (a page: its canvas; without rootId: the canvas, or the first page), rendered by the same engine as the canvas and the export. path writes the PNG under the screenshot directory (the database directory's screenshots/, or PAPRIKA_SCREENSHOTS); a path that leaves that directory is refused. With path the result is {path, width, height, url} and no image bytes; url is /api/screenshot/<id>. Without path the image is returned as before, plus url. mode paints the subtree in that theme mode (light, dark, …); omitted, a subtree keeps the mode it inherits from its frame or page. A missing or mismatched Chromium returns the command: pnpm --filter @paprika/e2e exec playwright install chromium.

tools.name: draw_diagram
tools.title: Draw a diagram
tools.description: Draws a flowchart-style diagram in one atomic write: each node becomes a shape (rect, ellipse, diamond, triangle or note, with text inside) and each edge a connector that stays attached when shapes move. Nodes without x and y are laid out in layers following the edges (direction down or right), to the right of the parent's existing content. Edges default to elbow routing (also straight, rounded, curve) with an arrow at the end; they may also point at existing nodes by id, and carry a label ("yes", "no") drawn halfway along the route.

tools.name: import_image
tools.title: Import image
tools.description: Places a raster image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or GIF) as an image node sized from the file's natural size (JPEG EXIF rotation applied). src is a data URL or a local file path: a path must resolve, symlinks included, inside an allowed directory (PAPRIKA_IMPORT_DIRS, default: the server's working directory; a relative path is taken from the first one). Files over 3500000 bytes are refused. The format comes from the bytes, not the extension. The original bytes are embedded unchanged, so an animated GIF, WebP or AVIF stays animated on the canvas and in HTML exports (render_screenshot captures one frame; warnings says so). width is a maximum: a larger image is scaled down keeping its ratio, a smaller one is never enlarged. Returns ids, roots and created in the same shape as create_nodes. The text is that JSON plus one readable line per root. The image honors place: "free" when x and y are omitted (right of the page content, gap 80), "below", "right", {near, side}, or "none" for the given x/y.

tools.description: Resamples an image node's pixels (or creates a node from src) to a named preset or a custom size, without Chromium. tools.name: duplicate_nodes
tools.title: Duplicate nodes
tools.description: Duplicates nodes with their whole subtree in one undo step (new ids; instances stay instances of the same component, scale multiplies their scale; connectors between duplicated nodes point at the copies, the others keep their ends). Each copy goes in its source's parent. With no offset, place defaults to the right of the source (gap 80) so the copy does not land on it; place is "free" | "below" | "right" | {near, side} | "none", and an explicit offset nudges x and y. scale grows or shrinks the copy from its own top-left corner: sizes, children positions, text size, strokes, radius, shadow, gap and padding; hug/fill stay. props is written on each copy's root (for example {mode: "dark"} for a light/dark pair). Returns copies (one id per source) and map (every source node to its copy), plus ids, roots and created in the same shape as create_nodes. The text is that JSON plus one readable line per root.

offset.description: Distance of each copy from its source, on x and y, in the parent's coordinates (default 40; 0 puts it on top)

parentId.description: Parent of the copies (null = canvas level; default: each source's parent)

scale.description: Multiplier for sizes, spacing, text and instance scale (default 1)

props.description: Fields written on each copy's root, e.g. {mode: "dark"}; id, type, parentId, children, sourceId and instanceOf are refused

tools.name: list_pins
tools.title: List pins (requests from the human)
tools.description: Pins are requests the human left on the canvas with the "Point for the AI" tool: a node or an area plus a text saying what to do there. Read them first when the human says "do the pins", and whenever a result carries openPins. Each pin has nodeId (or only region, for an area), region in canvas coordinates, pageId and text. status: open (default: open and claimed), claimed, resolved or all. Flow: claim_pin, do the work with the usual tools, then resolve_pin with a short reply. Pins are not nodes: they are not in the document, the export or the undo history.
